A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DBP attack study by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet attack evaluations in Tables 1–4, plus DiffAttack evaluations and attack-image analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds evaluations involving MimicDiffusion, an adversarially trained classifier and a GDMP configuration matched to the DiffHammer comparison.

M1.justification: DiffGrad's adjoint correction, checkpointing, reproducible randomness and guidance gradients remain unchanged, as do LF's optimizable filters and perceptual objective. Second-order guidance differentiation was already documented in v1 Appendix B.1. The new evaluations do not establish a changed attack procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 and ImageNet adversarial image classification under single-purification and majority-vote settings. V2 adds defense and classifier configurations within this coverage. The 10-class ImageNet subset is mentioned only when describing DiffHammer's work.

E2.justification: Sections 4.5–4.6 add MimicDiffusion as an evaluated defense and numerical comparisons against the concurrent DiffHammer attack for DiffPure and GDMP. These substantially extend the comparison beyond the retained methods and foundational defenses in v1.

E3.justification: V2 explicitly reruns the GDMP comparison using the Song et al. (2021) score model to match DiffHammer, and adds MimicDiffusion and adversarially trained classifier configurations. The original sample counts, attack budgets, optimization iterations, EoT counts and majority-vote settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds a robustness check of LF against DiffPure with an adversarially trained WideResNet-28-10, reporting 0.78% robust accuracy. The earlier DiffAttack per-step-loss analysis, vote-count checks and StAdv image-quality analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run variability. EoT sampling, the theoretical gradient-variance argument and the noise-sampler seed description are retained without a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values. V2 adds MimicDiffusion robust accuracies of 2.73%/4.3% under SP and 25.78%/27.73% under MV for WideResNet-28-10/70-16, respectively; the adversarially trained classifier result of 0.78%; and DiffHammer comparisons. Its new GDMP result of 5.47% uses a different score model, so it is not an improvement over the original table entry under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix B reformulate and relocate v1 Section 4.1's existing argument. The path-distribution objective, smoothness assumption, gradient-expectation identity and central-limit reasoning remain substantively the same, as do the DDPM equivalence and guidance-gradient derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that adaptive attacks undermine DBP's purification rationale, corrected gradients expose its vulnerability, and LF defeats its remaining majority-vote robustness. DiffBreak was already introduced in v1, and the conclusion about current DBP's inadequacy remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific explanations attributing MimicDiffusion's reported robustness to missing guidance derivatives and disputing DiffHammer's expectation-maximization rationale. It also explicitly limits the MimicDiffusion evaluation to CIFAR-10. Earlier interpretations concerning stochasticity, LF perturbations and StAdv's visual limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.6 identifies the alternative score-model source used for the additional GDMP comparison. Existing pseudocode, LF hyperparameters, A100 hardware information and toolkit access are retained. Appendix E largely relocates v1's model settings, and dropping '.git' from the repository URL does not change access.

R1.justification: The dedicated MimicDiffusion and DiffHammer sections substantially extend research positioning, explaining how DiffGrad differs from a recent defense and a concurrent attack. V2 also adds Foolbox as toolkit context and removes several background citations alongside shortened introductory discussion.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper around the existing DiffBreak toolkit and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and method exposition. It integrates the threat model into the background, moves the full theoretical argument and implementation explanations into appendices, and adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The document is broadly reformatted with a ruled title, running headers, repositioned and resized tables, and retypeset algorithm blocks. Figure 1 uses a different raster rendering. All appendix attack images are retained, with Figures S1–S18 renumbered as Figures 2–19.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical case through the MimicDiffusion evaluation, the adversarially trained classifier check and the GDMP comparison that explicitly matches DiffHammer's score model. These address additional questions about applicability and competitiveness. The gains are limited extensions of an otherwise retained method, original results and appendix evidence.
